sites.name: Anchor Wreck

s1.quote: Anchor Wreck … 6 to 35 meters … Moderate … Intermediate … a shallow anchor resting at around 6 meters

s2.quote: the large rusty anchor that is in 6m of water at the start of the reef wall … the majority of the wreck is in between 35 to 50m

s3.quote: Anchor Wreck … 5 to 45 m … between about 25 and 45 m

highlights.text: Large coral-encrusted anchor in the shallows
Wall continuing past 30 m

summary.text: A Menjangan wall dive named for a big rusty anchor resting at about 6 m. The wall drops well past 30 m, and the actual wreck lies deep at roughly 35-50 m, so most guides stay on the reef.

sites.depthNote: Anchor at ~6 m on the wall; main wreck about 35-50 m

s1.quote: Max Depth: 25 meters … Typical Current: Mild to Strong … this site can be tackled by less experienced divers as well as the more experienced

highlights.text: Sheltered lagoon and swim-through lined with sea fans
Giant sponge barrels on steep walls
Napoleon wrasse, bumphead parrotfish, pygmy seahorses

s1.quote: MELASTI Current: 0 – small Depth: 5 – 15 meters Marine life: Muck diver's heaven!

s2.quote: Melasti … 3–20 meters … All levels – Beginner to Advanced … Usually calm, mild current possible

highlights.text: Frogfish, harlequin shrimp, nudibranchs, seahorses

summary.text: A sandy, coral-poor muck site on the Amed coast, calm and shallow, great for macro. Frogfish, harlequin shrimp, nudibranchs and seahorses are regular finds.

s1.quote: The dive starts at about 20 meters … 25 meters … Mild to Medium … The only wall dive in central Raja Ampat

s2.quote: 0.5m to 25m … suitable for all levels of divers, from beginners to seasoned experts

highlights.text: Many nudibranch species and macro life
Whip corals, gorgonians, sponges on the wall
Pygmy seahorses, blacktip sharks, fusiliers

summary.text: A coral-covered wall in the Dampier Strait with small caves and overhangs, mild to medium current and suitable for all levels. Known for macro life such as nudibranchs and pygmy seahorses.

s1.quote: main action between 6 and 18 m … the most reliable manta encounters in the park

s2.quote: AVG DEPTH: 12M Avg. Depth: 12m; Max Depth: 22m karang makassar/manta point - central(open water friendly) Famous for sightings of up to 50 manta rays, Makassar is a 2 km drift dive … Due to strong currents, many corals find it hard to hold on and grow

s3.quote: These places are not very deep (5 to 15 meters) … Currents can be moderate to strong

highlights.text: Reliable manta ray encounters at cleaning stations
Turtles, eagle rays, bamboo sharks

summary.text: Makassar Reef in Komodo is a shallow drift over rubble where manta rays gather at cleaning stations, with the main action at roughly 6-18 m. Accessible to open-water divers with good buoyancy.

sites.name: Japanese Shipwreck (Wreck)

s1.quote: Japanese Wreck … 5–40 m … The Japanese wreck rests at a depth of just 5 m

s2.quote: Japanese Wreck … 5–30 meters … Intermediate … Calm to mild current, surge possible in shallow part

highlights.text: Macro life: pygmy seahorses, nudibranchs, ghost pipefish

summary.text: A small wreck lying in only about 5 m of water on the Amed coast, with a reef slope falling beyond it. Mild current and good macro life, including pygmy seahorses and ghost pipefish.

sites.depthNote: Wreck rests at about 5 m; reef slope continues deeper

s1.quote: Mayhem … Intermediate – Advanced … 7m-30m … Mild to Strong … It is home to many species of fusiliers

highlights.text: Many fusiliers on the north and east sides

sites.name: Baung Penyu Bay / Turtle Neck / The Wall

s1.quote: DROP OFF (Baung Penyu) DIVE SITE Dive site info: Drop Off Type of Dive: Boat dive, sandy slope to wall Depth: 5–30 meters Visibility: Often 10–20 meters

s2.quote: Blue Lagoon … Baong Penyu … turtle's neck … Up to 22 meters … All levels

highlights.text: Feather stars and seahorses

s1.quote: Batu Belah … 3–40 m … the beautiful colourful reef full of sponge, gorgonians and fish

s2.quote: Batu Belah is a real pleasure for the eyes … Thresher sharks and Eagle rays are (occasionally) seen here

highlights.text: Sponge and gorgonian reef
Reef sharks; occasional threshers and eagle rays

s1.quote: Max Depth: 25 meters. Typical Current: Medium to Strong … the site is recommended for intermediate to experienced divers due to the sometimes-strong currents through the channel

s2.quote: Fam Slope Snorkelling Friendly Level : All Levels Depth : 2m-25m Current : None-Mild

highlights.text: Reliable drift along a long wall
Manta rays, giant trevally, pygmy seahorses, turtles

summary.text: A drift dive along one long wall with steep slopes on the east side of Keruo Island, Raja Ampat. Currents through the channel can be strong; mantas, trevally, turtles and pygmy seahorses are seen.

s1.quote: Close Encounters … 5 to 25 m … perfect for any level of diver

s2.quote: Close Encounters (East slope/West slope) Trip Time: 5 -10 minutes Currents: Nothing to Moderate Brief: Steep slopes down to 12 – 24 m depth, then sandy slopes down to 30 m. With a flat top reef at a depth of 4 m

highlights.text: Gentle slopes with coral bommies and schooling fish
Baby sharks under table corals; nooks and sponges on the east side

summary.text: A flat-topped reef off Pemuteran with gentle slopes and scattered coral bommies. Calm, camera-friendly conditions suit any level; turtles, trevally, cuttlefish and baby sharks under table corals.

s1.quote: Lao Lao … All Levels … 8m-25m … None-Mild … a perfect multi-level dive sight with a maximum depth of 25m
Gili Tepekong … 18 to 30+ meters … 20 to 30 meters … Strong currents, surges, occasional down current

s2.quote: Both Blue Hole and Canyon have some tough currents … with an additional 10-logged dives to dive at Gili Tepekong

highlights.text: Whitetip and blacktip reef sharks
Sweetlips, jacks and grouper; mola-mola

summary.text: An offshore islet off Candidasa with the Blue Hole and Canyon dive routes. Tough currents and surge restrict it to experienced divers, who may see reef sharks, large fish schools and sometimes mola-mola.

s1.quote: Blue Corner … Multilevel drop-off 20m to 45m … 50+ m … Expert … Low to really strong

s2.quote: Blue Corner … Advanced … 30+ m … This site offer some of the most extreme condition around the islands

s3.quote: certified divers with sufficient experience only – Blue Corner

highlights.text: Mola mola and pelagic encounters

summary.text: A deep drop-off off the north-west corner of Nusa Lembongan with some of the strongest conditions around the islands. Advanced to expert only; pelagics such as mola mola and bull rays can appear.

s1.quote: Dream Wall … 10 to 40 meters … Moderate to strong … Advanced

s2.quote: Top 5 m, median 15 m, bottom 30 m … a vertical wall that weaves in and out with lots of nooks and crannies to explore

highlights.text: Large gorgonian fans from about 10 m
Fusiliers and anthias along the wall

hazards.text: Deeper stretches can pick up current unpredictably

summary.text: A vertical wall on the north coast of Menjangan next to Coral Garden, with large fans from about 10 m down. Moderate to strong current on the deeper parts makes it an advanced dive.

s1.quote: Avg. Depth: 15m; Max Depth: 40m wainilu - central(open water friendly) Wainilu is Komodo's own mini 'Lembeh'

s2.quote: Wainilu is a lesser-known but exceptional dive site near Rinca Island

s3.quote: Wainilu A shallow macro and critter site with rubble, sand and patient treasure-hunting. Good buoyancy and slow diving are essential to protect the habitat. Muck / rubble Max 12m

highlights.text: Ribbon eels, mandarin fish, frogfish, nudibranchs

hazards.text: Silt stirs up easily; needs good buoyancy

summary.text: A muck and macro site near Rinca Island, a sandy slope with little coral that is often called a mini Lembeh. Open-water friendly, but silt stirs easily so buoyancy matters.

s1.quote: Ghost Bay (Café Garam) … 5–20 meters … All levels … Usually calm, light current possible

highlights.text: Ghost pipefish, mimic octopus, stonefish

s1.quote: Good Heart … 5–20 metres … Beginner to Intermediate

s2.quote: Good Heart … a slope that drops down deep into the channel between Trawangan and Meno

highlights.text: Healthy coral and biorock restoration structures
Frogfish, turtles and reef sharks

summary.text: The Gili Trawangan house-reef slope on the east side, dropping toward the Meno channel. Relaxed conditions, coral restoration structures, turtles, frogfish and reef sharks, with octopus on night dives.

s1.quote: Gili Mimpang … 16 to 30 meters … 20 to 30 meters … Strong currents, occasional drift

s2.quote: Sharks are often found deep down near the islands at around 25+ metres … around 30 metres visibility year round … the currents can be quite strong even for advanced divers

highlights.text: Whitetip, wobbegong and coral cat sharks
Mola mola August to October

summary.text: A trio of rocks off Candidasa known for sharks below about 25 m and clear water. Currents can be strong even for advanced divers; sunfish appear from August to October.

s1.quote: Bias Tugal (White Sand Beach) … 15–35 meters … 6 to 10 m … Usually calm; light current and surge possible

s2.quote: Bias Tugel … shallow 10 meters … 30 to 40 meters … currents here can be unpredictable

highlights.text: Green turtles, pygmy seahorses, nudibranchs
Macro life and schooling fish

summary.text: A coral plateau at 6-10 m dropping to 30 m or more on a white-sand bay near Padang Bai. Calm most days but currents can be unpredictable; turtles, nudibranchs and pygmy seahorses.

s1.quote: Bat Cave … 10 to 30 meters … Strong drift … Advanced

s2.quote: Bat Caves … 5 to 55 m … intermittent currents … the best opportunity to meet a reef shark

s3.quote: ranges from shallow 3-meter dives to deeper areas around 40 meters

highlights.text: Reef sharks and trevallies
Crevices and caves at 9-12 m

summary.text: A wall on Menjangan with crevices and caves around 9-12 m, named for bats in the surface cave. Currents are strong at times, bringing trevallies and reef sharks.

s1.quote: Bunutan … 15–50 m … Medium … Every dive is an amazing drift diving experience

s2.quote: Bunutan … 5–30+ meters … Advanced Open Water … Garden eels, barrel sponges, Morays, stingrays, reef sharks

highlights.text: Garden eels, barrel sponges, stingrays, reef sharks

summary.text: A drift dive along the Amed coast with garden eels, barrel sponges, stingrays and reef sharks. Current is moderate and usually runs parallel to shore; advanced open water is suggested.

s1.quote: Depth Range: 8–30m … Experience Level: Intermediate – Advanced … Best dived during slack tide or mild incoming currents

s2.quote: Police Corner A current-swept point in central Komodo with current-driven biodiversity, reef sharks, schooling fish and powerful scenery. A rewarding site for experienced divers. Point / drift Max 30m

highlights.text: Large overhang forming a cave-like cathedral
Whitetip reef sharks and bumphead parrotfish

summary.text: A current-swept slope in central Komodo with a large cave-like overhang. Best at slack or mild incoming tide; reef sharks, bumphead parrotfish and fusiliers draw advanced divers.
